P01-008.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the tile sign-act (4:1-4:3) from the lying and food-rationing sign-acts (4:4-4:17) as two units. How the sign-acts of chs 4-7 divide is an open question, and the 4:3/4:4 seam is its strongest form, so the rival and the mark behind it are weighed here. On the rival's far face the witness records a samekh after oshb:Ezek.4.3 (single-witness), and that verse closes on the sign-act colophon א֥וֹת הִ֖יא לְבֵ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Ezek.4.3), “This shall be a sign to the house of Israel” (web:Ezek.4.3), standing verse-final. On its near face, the candidate onset, oshb:Ezek.4.4 carries no formula whatever: MEASURED over the pointed Hebrew witness, no verse of ch 4 belongs to the messenger, utterance, recognition or word-event classes, the chapter's only counted members being the son-of-man address at 4:1 and 4:16 and the year-word non-datelines at 4:5-4:6. The colophon is not a close-role formula - oshb:Ezek.4.3 is absent from both the 81-verse utterance list and the 64-verse recognition family - so the verse before the candidate onset does not end on a verse-final utterance or recognition formula; and the addressee is unchanged across the seam, 2ms imperatives standing to the prophet on either side, so no change of addressee opens a sub-onset there either. A section mark alone never stands in for that verse-final close-role formula. The rival is therefore paragraph-grade, held on those grounds, and the samekh is disclosed for the alternative it corroborates rather than for this row. The openings, 4:3 included as the very verse the mark follows, divide this way: the titled sub-onset וְאַתָּ֤ה בֶן אָדָם֙ stands at 4:1 and again at 5:1, whereas bare וְאַתָּ֤ה without the title opens three interior stages - 4:3, 4:4 and 4:9 - so the text stages the siege-model, the iron pan, the two lying postures and the rationed food as one commanded act and not as separate commands (oshb:Ezek.4.1).
P01-008.boundary_rationale: Onset: 4:1 וְאַתָּ֤ה בֶן אָדָם֙ קַח לְךָ֣ לְבֵנָ֔ה (oshb:Ezek.4.1) (“You also, son of man, take a tile” (web:Ezek.4.1)), the 'and you, son of man' sub-onset that opens P2 (one of the book's 23 occurrences of that construction), immediately after the parent seam weighed at oshb:Ezek.3.27. The same siege-tile complex continues through the lying sign-acts at 4:4 and the food-rationing at 4:9 without a matching 'son of man' sub-onset at either point (both open with the bare 've'attah' alone), so all three stages read as one commanded symbolic act rather than three. At 4:8, וְהִנֵּ֛ה נָתַ֥תִּי עָלֶ֖יךָ עֲבוֹתִ֑ים (oshb:Ezek.4.8) (“Behold, I put ropes on you” (web:Ezek.4.8)) recurs the exact word from 3:25 on the far side of the parent seam, disclosed as continuity evidence already weighed at that seam. A second address at 4:16, בֶּן אָדָם֙ (oshb:Ezek.4.16), intensifies rather than restarts the act (“behold, I will break the staff of bread” (web:Ezek.4.16)). Close: 4:17, לְמַ֥עַן יַחְסְר֖וּ לֶ֣חֶם וָמָ֑יִם (oshb:Ezek.4.17) (“that they may lack bread and water” (web:Ezek.4.17)), with a pe recorded after it, before 5:1 opens a distinct sign-act with its own 'son of man' address.

P01-014.strongest_rejected_alternative: The single Ezek.7.5-Ezek.7.27 row, rejected on the 2mp recognition close and the doubled eye-not-sparing refrain at oshb:Ezek.7.9, whose five-word WEB rendering “My eye will not spare” (web:Ezek.7.4) stands at 7:4 and is contracted at 7:9. The WEB's own paragraph breaks inside this stretch (7:15, 7:23) may stand as a secondary, tier-4 consideration only: none of them coincides with a word-event, messenger formula or set-your-face device — they are translation-layer paragraphing — so the entire stretch still reads as one intensifying doom-poem to its own recognition-formula close at 7:27.

P02-001.literature_type_guess: temple-vision onset: the transported hand-of-YHWH scene and what the prophet is first shown, “the seat of the image of jealousy, which provokes to jealousy” (web:Ezek.8.3)

P02-002.strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this row through 8:18 (treating all four temple-tour tableaux as one row) was weighed: the text supports it by the repeated 'again see' device running through 8:6, 8:13, 8:15 and 8:17, but a twelve-verse row (MEASURED: web:Ezek.8.7-Ezek.8.18 is 12 verses, counted on the WEB face) with no internal formula anchor at all would understate the four distinct transport-marked scenes; the transport verbs at 8:7, 8:14 and 8:16 are kept as row-opening evidence instead.

P02-003.boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.8.14 וַיָּבֵ֣א אֹתִ֗י אֶל פֶּ֨תַח֙ שַׁ֣עַר בֵּית יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֖ר אֶל הַצָּפ֑וֹנָה וְהִנֵּה שָׁם֙ הַנָּשִׁ֣ים יֹֽשְׁב֔וֹת מְבַכּ֖וֹת אֶת הַתַּמּֽוּז, a third transport (“he brought me to the door of the gate of Yahweh’s house” (web:Ezek.8.14)) opening the Tammuz-weeping tableau; a samekh follows this very verse (single-witness), which is disclosed as evidence that could instead argue a shorter row ending at 8:15 (see rejected alternative). The row is extended through a second transport at oshb:Ezek.8.16 וַיָּבֵ֣א אֹתִ֗י אֶל חֲצַ֣ר בֵּית יְהוָה֮ הַפְּנִימִית֒ וְהִנֵּה פֶ֜תַח הֵיכַ֣ל יְהוָ֗ה בֵּ֤ין הָֽאוּלָם֙ וּבֵ֣ין הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ כְּעֶשְׂרִ֥ים וַחֲמִשָּׁ֖ה אִ֑ישׁ אֲחֹ֨רֵיהֶ֜ם אֶל הֵיכַ֤ל יְהוָה֙ וּפְנֵיהֶ֣ם קֵ֔דְמָה וְהֵ֛מָּה מִשְׁתַּחֲוִיתֶ֥ם קֵ֖דְמָה לַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ (the sun-worshippers, “about twenty-five men… their backs toward Yahweh’s temple” (web:Ezek.8.16)) because a cut before 8:16 would leave a row under three verses, and such a row is held only for a complete word-event unit — that ground is stated and weighed in the rejected alternative, and no mark-absence is offered for or against any seam here. Close: oshb:Ezek.8.18 וְגַם אֲנִי֙ אֶעֱשֶׂ֣ה בְחֵמָ֔ה לֹֽא תָח֥וֹס עֵינִ֖י וְלֹ֣א אֶחְמֹ֑ל וְקָרְא֤וּ בְאָזְנַי֙ ק֣וֹל גָּד֔וֹל וְלֹ֥א אֶשְׁמַ֖ע אוֹתָֽם is the wrath declaration — “I will also deal in wrath… I will not hear them” (web:Ezek.8.18) — a narrative and thematic close (the fourfold tableau's climax) rather than a recognition or utterance refrain; oshb:Ezek.9.1 opens the next scene with the loud-voiced cry that sets the executioners in motion, which is the strongest available onset-side confirmation that 8:18 is where the temple-tour proper ends.
P02-003.strongest_rejected_alternative: The live rival is a seam at 8:15/8:16, weighed here face by face and held. Its far face is the pointer close at oshb:Ezek.8.15, the third of this tour's forward-pointing 'you will again see' transitions (8:6, 8:13, 8:15); its near face, the candidate onset, is oshb:Ezek.8.16, a verse of the closed transport class and one of the tour's scene seams, which fall at 8:5, 8:7, 8:14 and 8:16. The rival is therefore licensed on both faces and it is not dismissed. The row holds because a licensed driver yields a row under three verses only when it is a complete word-event unit: a cut before 8:16 leaves 8:14-8:15, which MEASURED on the WEB face is only 2 verses (the remainder 8:16-8:18 has 3) and is not a complete word-event unit. The samekh recorded on MT 8:14 (single-witness) is entered as support for the alternative it favours and no wider: a mark is recorded on the verse it stands after, so honouring it as a close would end this row at its own onset verse, 8:14, a one-verse row that is no complete word-event unit, and a section break carries corroborating weight only, ranking below every licensed driver.

P02-016.device_notes: No K/Q note or paseq falls in 13:1-9 (single-witness). P03-007.strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this row through 16:58 (the whole sisters-and-Samaria comparison as one span) was weighed and not taken: a samekh follows MT 16:50, single witness, and the Sodom comparison’s content is complete at that verse. Across that seam MT 16:51 carries no licensed text signal: it opens on the conjunction with Samaria, וְשֹׁ֣מְר֔וֹן כַּחֲצִ֥י (oshb:Ezek.16.51), the sister already named at 16:46, an opening found in this verse alone (sweep: 1 verse), and MEASURED against every counted onset-formula class - word-event, messenger, son-of-man address, set-your-face, hand-of-YHWH, transport and dateline - it carries none. That cross-seam continuity argues against the cut, so the merge through 16:58 is held as a live alternative on the mark and the content close rather than refused on the bytes.
P03-007.device_notes: A Ketiv/Qere note stands at MT 16:47 (oshb:Ezek.16.47, single-witness): the running text reads the ketiv עשיתי in place of the Qere עָשִׂ֑ית; no other K/Q note falls in 16:44-50. The witness records no paseq and no editors' note in this span.

P04-011.boundary_rationale: Every reference in this row touches MT ch 21 and is written dual. Onset: the and-you-son-of-man-prophesy sub-onset at web:Ezek.21.28 = oshb:Ezek.21.33 (וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן אָדָ֗ם הִנָּבֵ֤א וְאָֽמַרְתָּ֙ כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֔ה אֶל בְּנֵ֥י עַמּ֖וֹן וְאֶל חֶרְפָּתָ֑ם וְאָמַרְתָּ֗ חֶ֣רֶב חֶ֤רֶב פְּתוּחָה֙ לְטֶ֣בַח מְרוּטָ֔ה לְהָכִ֖יל לְמַ֥עַן בָּרָֽק), carrying its own messenger formula and a foreign addressee — the WEB reads it “concerning the children of Ammon, and concerning their reproach” (web:Ezek.21.28 = oshb:Ezek.21.33) — an addressee-class shift from the Judean material closed just before it. Close: the emphatic I-YHWH-have-spoken formula at web:Ezek.21.32 = oshb:Ezek.21.37 (לָאֵ֤שׁ תִּֽהְיֶה֙ לְאָכְלָ֔ה דָּמֵ֥ךְ יִהְיֶ֖ה בְּת֣וֹךְ הָאָ֑רֶץ לֹ֣א תִזָּכֵ֔רִי כִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבַּֽרְתִּי), with a pe immediately after.

P05-004.device_notes: Cap deviation disclosed: 21 verses, above the 7-10 typical / 14-16 measured-block cap, held medium_low rather than forcing an unsupported internal cut. The interior carries the samekh after MT 23:10 and the close seam the samekh after MT 23:21, both disclosed above, so a mark is disclosed at the onset seam, in the interior and at the close seam alike. In this witness a setumah (closed section) is written SAMEKH and a petuchah (open section) is written PE. The mark on MT 22:31 is a PE, marking an open section, not a closed one. A licensed text signal outranks a section mark, so the mark is weak corroboration and carries nothing on its own; this onset rests on the strict word-event formula at 23:1.

P06-009.boundary_rationale: Onset: 27:1 opens with the strict word-event formula, "וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר" (oshb:Ezek.27.1). 27:2 supplies the genre command to the prophet, "וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן אָדָ֔ם שָׂ֥א עַל צֹ֖ר קִינָֽה" — “take up a lamentation over Tyre” (web:Ezek.27.2, WEB) — the imperative-to-the-prophet plus קִינָֽה (oshb:Ezek.27.2) noun, the clearest lament_qinah byte-anchor in this span, in contrast to the reported-speech קִינָה֙ (oshb:Ezek.26.17) inside Ezek.26.17. In the WEB, “You, son of man, take up a lamentation over Tyre;” (web:Ezek.27.2). Close (both sides): 27:36 ends "סֹֽחֲרִים֙ בָּ֣עַמִּ֔ים שָׁרְק֖וּ עָלָ֑יִךְ בַּלָּה֣וֹת הָיִ֔ית וְאֵינֵ֖ךְ עַד עוֹלָֽם" (oshb:Ezek.27.36) with a SAMEKH immediately after and no recognition/utterance/"I YHWH have spoken" formula in the verse; the close is argued from the parashah mark plus the chapter's own colophon-like terminal clause (the WEB renders it “You have come to a terrible end, and you will be no more.”, web:Ezek.27.36, WEB), not from a formula. This is treated as ONE row for the whole chapter because a qinah-labelled unit is never split, and the whole chapter is one 36-verse qinah; the internal trade list at 27:12-24 is itself a list never cut inside, and no formula licenses an internal seam. One formula does stand inside the chapter: MEASURED from the pointed Hebrew witness, the long-form messenger formula stands inside MT 27:3 (oshb:Ezek.27.3). It licenses nothing - it sits mid-verse inside the commissioned speech frame. A messenger formula opens a sub-onset only when the addressee changes or the verse before it ENDS on a verse-final close-role formula, and neither holds here: the addressee does not change (Tyre throughout), and MT 27:2 does not END on a close-role formula. MEASURED over the same witness, that is the chapter’s ONLY internal messenger formula, and the word-event formula occurs only at the onset, MT 27:1. Behind, 26:21 closed the Tyre-siege chapter on the utterance formula + SAMEKH; ahead, 28:1 opens a fresh strict word-event onset for the prince-of-Tyre oracle.
P06-009.strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting at 27:11/27:12 (the shift from the ship-building description to the trade list) or at 27:25/27:26 (end of the trade list, resumption of the poetic lament proper) to bring the row nearer the 7-10 verse target was rejected: neither point carries a word-event, messenger-formula, or parashah mark, both are plain `|q` line continuations, and a qinah-labelled unit is never split, regardless of length; the size cap is disclosed instead of forcing an unmarked internal cut. That negative holds in the witness: MEASURED in this witness, no parashah mark stands on MT 27:11, 27:12, 27:25 or 27:26 - the chapter's only mark is the samekh after MT 27:36 (single-witness) - and MEASURED from the pointed Hebrew witness neither the messenger formula (chapter-internal only at MT 27:3) nor the word-event formula (only at MT 27:1) falls at any of those four points.
P06-009.device_notes: WHOLE-CHAPTER SPAN (cap disclosure): 36 verses (MEASURED over the pointed Hebrew witness) against the 7-10 verses-per-row target, which is the benchmark that governs this row; the 14-16 verse allowance is NOT available here, because that allowance belongs only to the measured-and-listed blocks, named by chapter, and this chapter is not among them; held here at medium_low with the cap disclosed rather than an unmarked internal cut, since the qinah is never split and the internal trade list (12-24) is never cut inside. P08-001.boundary_rationale: Onset: the word-event formula opens this unit and the parent, Ezek.33.1 וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Ezek.33.1) — one of the book's 39 strict word-event onsets and a hard seam; it also carries the P6/P7 seam at 32:32/33:1, corroborated by a pe mark following MT 32:32 (single-witness) immediately before this unit's onset, since the addressee returns from the nations “to the children of your people” (web:Ezek.33.2) in the next verse, Ezek.33.2 בֶּן אָדָ֗ם דַּבֵּ֤ר אֶל בְּנֵֽי עַמְּךָ֙ וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם אֶ֕רֶץ כִּֽי אָבִ֥יא עָלֶ֖יהָ חָ֑רֶב וְלָקְח֨וּ עַם הָאָ֜רֶץ אִ֤ישׁ אֶחָד֙ מִקְצֵיהֶ֔ם וְנָתְנ֥וּ אֹת֛וֹ לָהֶ֖ם לְצֹפֶֽה (oshb:Ezek.33.2). Close: the row ends where the watchman analogy itself ends, at Ezek.33.9 וְ֠אַתָּה כִּֽי הִזְהַ֨רְתָּ רָשָׁ֤ע מִדַּרְכּוֹ֙ לָשׁ֣וּב מִמֶּ֔נָּה וְלֹא שָׁ֖ב מִדַּרְכּ֑וֹ ה֚וּא בַּעֲוֺנ֣וֹ יָמ֔וּת וְאַתָּ֖ה נַפְשְׁךָ֥ הִצַּֽלְתָּ (oshb:Ezek.33.9), corroborated by a samekh mark following that verse (single-witness, disclosed). No recognition or utterance refrain closes this sub-unit — the close is topical, not formulaic, and is disclosed as such rather than claimed as a formula match. Both sides weighed: onset side carries the hard-seam word-event plus the addressee return; close side carries the samekh corroboration at oshb:Ezek.33.9, immediately before the topical shift at Ezek.33.10, where 'son of man' reopens with a distinct target (“the house of Israel” (web:Ezek.33.10)) and a quoted popular saying, the disputation-oracle device that opens at Ezek.33.10.

P08-002.boundary_rationale: Onset: the sub-onset 'son of man' at Ezek.33.10 וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן אָדָ֗ם אֱמֹר֙ אֶל בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כֵּ֤ן אֲמַרְתֶּם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר כִּֽי פְשָׁעֵ֥ינוּ וְחַטֹּאתֵ֖ינוּ עָלֵ֑ינוּ וּבָ֛ם אֲנַ֥חְנוּ נְמַקִּ֖ים וְאֵ֥יךְ נִֽחְיֶֽה (oshb:Ezek.33.10) opens with the quoted popular saying it will refute, immediately following the samekh-marked close at oshb:Ezek.33.9. That re-address turns the speech from the prophet-directed watchman charge back to the people and is licensed as an onset, while the far face behind it carries that samekh and no formula, a mark only. An oath-plus-utterance combination follows at Ezek.33.11 אֱמֹ֨ר אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם חַי אָ֣נִי נְאֻ֣ם אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה אִם אֶחְפֹּץ֙ בְּמ֣וֹת הָרָשָׁ֔ע כִּ֣י אִם בְּשׁ֥וּב רָשָׁ֛ע מִדַּרְכּ֖וֹ וְחָיָ֑ה שׁ֣וּבוּ שׁ֜וּבוּ מִדַּרְכֵיכֶ֧ם הָרָעִ֛ים וְלָ֥מָּה תָמ֖וּתוּ בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Ezek.33.11), carrying its own pe mark; this is disclosed as close-grade material that is NOT final here, because the same disputation continues through a second 'son of man' sub-onset at Ezek.33.12 restating the principle for “the children of your people” (web:Ezek.33.12) and on through the righteous/wicked case-pairs of 33.14-19. Close: a second pe mark follows Ezek.33.20 וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֕ם לֹ֥א יִתָּכֵ֖ן דֶּ֣רֶךְ אֲדֹנָ֑י אִ֧ישׁ כִּדְרָכָ֛יו אֶשְׁפּ֥וֹט אֶתְכֶ֖ם בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Ezek.33.20), which restates the people's complaint from 33.17 -- the four pointed words לֹ֥א יִתָּכֵ֖ן דֶּ֣רֶךְ אֲדֹנָ֑י stand byte-identical in both verses (oshb:Ezek.33.17, oshb:Ezek.33.20; WLC/OSHB, single witness) -- and then adds YHWH's verdict (“I will judge every one of you after his ways” (web:Ezek.33.20)), which stands at 33.20 only and has no counterpart anywhere in 33.17, marking the disputation's true end. EXTRACTED from this witness's markup, with independent verification UNAVAILABLE, MT 33:20 carries no sof pasuq; the editors' note stands in its place, 'We read punctuation in L differently from BHS,' immediately before the pe (single witness). No boundary is argued from the absent mark, only from the pe that follows and the topical restatement it closes. That near face is a verdict clause with no formula of its own -- the discourse close of the disputation, corroborated by the pe that follows and by no formula -- while the far face past it opens the next unit on the dateline at 33:21. A close seam whose near face is a discourse close without a formula is what this row's medium_low records, whatever stands on its far face.

P08-010.boundary_rationale: Onset: the witness records a pe after MT 35:15 (single-witness), at the seam this unit opens on. The sub-onset 'and you, son of man' at Ezek.36.1 וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן אָדָ֔ם הִנָּבֵ֖א אֶל הָרֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְאָ֣מַרְתָּ֔ הָרֵי֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל שִׁמְע֖וּ דְּבַר יְהוָֽה (oshb:Ezek.36.1) pivots the shared Ezek.35.1 word-event frame from Edom “to the mountains of Israel,” (web:Ezek.36.1) the second side of a two-sided unit shared with Ezek.35.1-Ezek.35.15. A cluster of six messenger-formula occurrences runs Ezek.36.2 through Ezek.36.7 (verified directly from these verses' own bytes); this cluster does not cut internally, since the addressee (the mountains) never changes and no refrain-grade close intervenes between any two occurrences. A samekh mark falls after Ezek.36.4, mid-cluster; disclosed as non-cutting for the same reason. Close: a 2mp recognition-family clause at Ezek.36.11 וְהִרְבֵּיתִ֧י עֲלֵיכֶ֛ם אָדָ֥ם וּבְהֵמָ֖ה וְרָב֣וּ וּפָר֑וּ וְהוֹשַׁבְתִּ֨י אֶתְכֶ֜ם כְּקַדְמֽוֹתֵיכֶ֗ם וְהֵטִֽבֹתִי֙ מֵרִאשֹׁ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם וִֽידַעְתֶּ֖ם כִּֽי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה (oshb:Ezek.36.11) (wider family, disclosed), followed by Ezek.36.12 וְהוֹלַכְתִּי֩ עֲלֵיכֶ֨ם אָדָ֜ם אֶת עַמִּ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וִֽירֵשׁ֔וּךָ וְהָיִ֥יתָ לָהֶ֖ם לְנַחֲלָ֑ה וְלֹא תוֹסִ֥ף ע֖וֹד לְשַׁכְּלָֽם (oshb:Ezek.36.12) restating the inheritance promise and a samekh mark, close the row immediately before a fresh messenger formula reopens at Ezek.36.13, itself licensed as a cutting seam by the addressee change from this row's 2mp/2ms address (“you,” the mountains) to the 2fs address (“you,” feminine singular, the land) that opens at Ezek.36.13.

P09-002.device_notes: Operative-category disclosure: the 37.15-28 span is anchored as sign_act (the commanded stick action of 37.16-20), but its interpretation at 37.21-28 carries the salvation_oracle burden (gather/return, the covenant of peace at 37.26, ‘my servant David’ and ‘my sanctuary’ devices) -- a one-clause category deviation rather than a split: the pe behind it at 37.14 and the samekh closing it at 37.28 are the row's only framing marks, and the addressee stays constant across both halves. 37.16 is a doubled ketiv/qere verse: two notes on one verse, each written חברו (oshb:Ezek.37.16, ketiv), and each read as the same consonantal word under different pointing -- the first note reads חֲבֵרָ֑יו and the second חֲבֵרָֽיו, the two differing by exactly one codepoint, U+0591 HEBREW ACCENT ETNAHTA in the first against U+05BD HEBREW POINT METEG in the second (MEASURED by diffing the two notes of the K/Q apparatus at this verse, codepoint by codepoint; WLC/OSHB, single witness), and 37.19 carries one further note on the same word (written חברו (oshb:Ezek.37.19, ketiv), read חֲבֵרָ֑יו (oshb:Ezek.37.19, Qere)); 37.22 carries a further K/Q note in this span (written יהיה (oshb:Ezek.37.22, ketiv), read יִֽהְיוּ (oshb:Ezek.37.22, Qere)). A boundary is never argued from any of these Qere readings; they are disclosed as textual-variant sites only.

P09-008.device_notes: MT 39.12 and 39.14 both read חֳדָשִֽׁים (oshb:Ezek.39.12) / חֳדָשִׁ֖ים (oshb:Ezek.39.14) -- ‘months’, a stated DURATION (seven months of burying, then a further search: “After the end of seven months they will search.” (web:Ezek.39.14)) -- not a calendar date and not a dateline; this span opens no oracle and is never read as a unit onset. 39.11 carries one paseq (count-only, single-witness); no K/Q falls in this span. 39.11 also carries an OSHB editorial note recording a ketiv/qere editorial decision (single-witness apparatus; no specific variant reading is asserted from it).

P10-004.boundary_rationale: Onset side: 40:20 opens the outer court's gate circuit on a measure notice rather than a vayiqtol verb, מָדַ֥ד אָרְכּ֖וֹ וְרָחְבּֽוֹ (oshb:Ezek.40.20) 'he measured its length and its width', immediately after the outer court's whole-court span closes at 40:19. The row measures the outer north gate (40:20-23), keyed to the first gate's own dimensions, הָיָ֔ה כְּמִדַּ֖ת הַשַּׁ֣עַר הָרִאשׁ֑וֹן (oshb:Ezek.40.21) “the measure of the first gate” (web:Ezek.40.21), a phrase standing only at 40:21 in the chapter (sweep: 1 verse), and the outer south gate (40:24-27), keyed instead by כַּמִּדּ֖וֹת הָאֵֽלֶּה (oshb:Ezek.40.24) 'according to these measurements', a refrain recurring at 40:24, 40:28, 40:29, 40:32, 40:33 and 40:35 (sweep: 6 verses across chapter 40); the row carries four of the ch-40 doubled K/Q verses (40:21, 40:22, 40:24, 40:26) plus a single note at 40:25, every one the recurring ketiv-defective/qere-plene 3ms possessive-suffix pattern on chambers, posts, porches, windows and palm trees, never on the cubit figures themselves. A transport verb sits inside this row at 40:24, וַיּוֹלִכֵ֨נִי֙ דֶּ֣רֶךְ הַדָּר֔וֹם (oshb:Ezek.40.24) “He led me toward the south” (web:Ezek.40.24), moving from the north gate to the south gate within the same outer court; it is disclosed as intra-row sub-onset texture, not the row seam, because it changes compass direction but not court. Close side: 40:27 ends the south outer gate on its hundred-cubit span to the inner court's south gate, וַיָּ֨מָד מִשַּׁ֧עַר אֶל הַשַּׁ֛עַר דֶּ֥רֶךְ הַדָּר֖וֹם מֵאָ֥ה אַמּֽוֹת (oshb:Ezek.40.27), immediately before 40:28's court-change transport verb. The seam at 40:27/40:28 turns on a location change -- the next verse's transport verb crosses from the outer court into the inner court -- unlike the compass-direction transport at 40:24 inside this row.

P10-010.boundary_rationale: Onset side: 42:1 opens with a double transport verb, וַיּוֹצִאֵ֗נִי אֶל הֶֽחָצֵר֙ הַחִ֣יצוֹנָ֔ה ... וַיְבִאֵ֣נִי אֶל הַלִּשְׁכָּ֗ה (oshb:Ezek.42.1) “he brought me out into the outer court” (web:Ezek.42.1) ... “Then he brought me into the room” (web:Ezek.42.1) -- the strongest onset in the span after 40:1 and 43:1 -- moving the tour to the priests' chambers, first north-side (42:1-9) then, by parallel description, south-side (42:10-12). Close side: 42:13-14 supplies the row's function, delivered as a genuine speak-formula, וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֗י (oshb:Ezek.42.13) 'he said to me': these are the holy chambers where the priests “eat the most holy things” (web:Ezek.42.13) and must change garments before approaching the people -- a law-toned close inside a measurement row, disclosed rather than reclassified. Both the double transport at onset and the speak-formula at close are tier-1 devices, a stronger onset-and-close pairing than a bare content shift would give, despite the total absence of parashah corroboration in these chapters.

P10-015.boundary_rationale: Onset side: 43:18 opens on a said-to-me verse, וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֗י, and then carries בֶּן אָדָם֙ כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה (oshb:Ezek.43.18) 'son of man, thus says the Lord YHWH' -- one of the book's 122 messenger-formula verses, and the clearest speech-onset here after the throne declaration of 43:1-9 -- introducing the altar's dedication ordinances. The utterance formula נְאֻ֛ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה (oshb:Ezek.43.19) appears mid-unit at 43:19, read as paragraph-final rather than row-final since the seven-day consecration instructions continue without interruption. The row carries the young-bull sin offering, the blood rite on the horns and corners, the second-day goat, the seven-day consecration, and closes at 43:27 on the same utterance formula, וְרָצִ֣אתִי אֶתְכֶ֔ם נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהֹוִֽה (oshb:Ezek.43.27) “Then I will accept you,’ says the Lord Yahweh” (web:Ezek.43.27), this time genuinely row-final. Close side: immediately after that utterance the verse carries two consecutive samekh marks, the sole doubled occurrence among the book's marked verses (sweep: 183 verses) -- making 43:27 the best-attested close available and the strongest evidence for ending it exactly here. Both sides converge unusually cleanly here: a messenger-formula onset opposite an utterance-plus-doubled-mark close.

P11-001.device_notes: MT 44.3 carries an OSHB 'anomalous form' editorial note, single-witness apparatus, disclosed and not argued as boundary evidence. Parashah marks in three directions, MEASURED in this witness, where a mark is recorded ON the verse it FOLLOWS. Onset seam: corroboration IS present -- two consecutive samekh marks follow Ezek.43.27, the verse immediately before this row's first verse, and this row's own rationale argues from them. Interior, Ezek.44.1-Ezek.44.3: no mark. Close seam: no mark follows Ezek.44.4; the next mark in the book is the pe following Ezek.44.14. So the span does carry parashah corroboration, at its onset seam though not in its interior or at its close seam; each mark is single-witness and corroborates only, never deciding a seam alone. Held at medium_low, weighing the alternative close at 44.3 (the shut gate alone) against the transport-and-prostration close at 44.4.

P11-003.device_notes: MT 44.24 is one of the book's 23 doubled K/Q-note verses (two notes in the K/Q apparatus), disclosed as a textual-variant site; a boundary is never argued from it. MT 44.24 also carries a separate OSHB editorial note ('we read one or more consonants in L differently from BHS'), single-witness, disclosed. This row's 17-verse length exceeds the typical 7-10 verse density and the measured/listed-block cap of 14-16, and is disclosed rather than forced into a cut at an unmarked point. The Ezek.44.15 and Ezek.44.27 utterance occurrences are disclosed as paragraph-internal texture; only the Ezek.44.31 pe is treated as the row's own close.

P11-013.boundary_rationale: Onset: no formula device opens Ezek.48.30 (“These are the exits of the city” (web:Ezek.48.30)); the seam behind it at 48.29/48.30 is argued from the Ezek.48.29 close (utterance + pe) and the topic shift from the tribal-portion summary to the city gates. The row covers the city's four sides, their measurements and named gates (30-34), and the book's final verse (35), the city's circumference and its new name. Close: the book's own end. No formula closes 48.35; no parashah mark is recorded after it, since none is possible on the book's last verse; a paseq is recorded within it (count-only, single-witness). This is disclosed as the row's own close condition rather than argued as a gap or omission.
